neutrality_rule: Operational edges are not lineage edges; outcome vectors are unfilled.

carrier_relation.question: How are source and target supports related at the protocol level?

values.same_support_reencoding: One support is retained while representation, coordinates, or packaging changes.
values.partially_overlapping_support: Source-side and target-side supports are separately typed but share components or jointly contribute during some interval.
values.disjoint_support: Source-side and target-side supports have no shared support component at the declared comparison level.

carrier_relation.blocked: Carrier relation does not determine transport, lineage, realization, or ontology.

change_mode.question: What operational mechanism changes source-side support into target-side support?

values.gradual_replacement: Support responsibility changes in multiple ordered stages.
values.abrupt_translation: A single or effectively unresolved stage maps a declared source record/package into target form.
values.checkpoint_restart: A retained record is used to activate a target after pause, shutdown, or absence.
values.live_migration: An active package is maintained while responsibility moves between concurrently operating supports.
values.destructive_scan: Source support/package is disabled or made unavailable as part of acquisition/reconstruction.
values.nondestructive_copy: A target is constructed while the source remains available for at least one stage.
values.distributed_extension: A package is extended across multiple supports without requiring a unique transfer instant.

change_mode.blocked: Mode names describe engineering order, not continuity verdicts.

source_fate.question: What happens operationally to source-side package support?

values.persists: Source support remains active and available after target activation.
values.degrades: Source contribution is progressively reduced or loses declared capability.
values.paused: Source dynamics are intentionally suspended while a recoverable record/support remains.
values.erased_before_activation: Source package/support is made unavailable before target activation.
values.erased_after_activation: Source package/support remains for a period after target activation and is then made unavailable.
values.remains_coupled: Source remains an active causal/resource component of the operating source-target assembly.

source_fate.blocked: Source destruction, persistence, or coupling does not by itself decide lineage.

target_timing.question: How is target activation temporally related to source activity?

values.continuous_overlap: Source and target have an interval of concurrent operation or contribution.
values.delayed_activation: Target activates after acquisition/construction, without a stipulated extended dormant gap.
values.temporal_gap: No active package is stipulated for a nonzero interval between source cessation/pause and target activation.
values.time_rescaled_activation: Target operation is related by an explicit non-unit clock map or time reparameterization.

target_timing.blocked: Temporal continuity or discontinuity does not define lineage by itself.

branching.question: What is the cardinality/topology of operational package episodes?

values.one_to_one: One designated source episode is connected operationally to one designated target episode.
values.one_to_many: One source episode produces or feeds multiple target/live continuation episodes.
values.many_to_one: Multiple source/branch episodes contribute to one target episode.
values.many_to_many: The protocol contains multiple source-side and target-side episodes or distributed pieces.

branching.blocked: Operational branching is not a lineage graph until a criterion supplies lineage edges.

bridge_dependence.question: What continuing bridge or protocol support is built into the scenario?

values.permanent: The source-target coupling/bridge remains part of the declared operating assembly.
values.temporary: The protocol schedules the bridge to end, but target autonomy is not stipulated.
values.removable: The setup exposes a well-defined withdrawal intervention; survival after withdrawal is left open.
values.externally_decoded: The claimed target-facing structure/readout requires a continuing external decoder or source process.

bridge_dependence.blocked: A removable bridge is not thereby safely removable; a permanent bridge is not thereby illegitimate.

fidelity.question: What kind of agreement is stipulated at the scenario's declared transfer granularity?

values.exact: Zero declared defect at the named granularity only.
values.lossy: Some declared source information/structure is omitted or changed.
values.error_corrected: A recovery/repair mechanism is part of the stipulated target construction.
values.residual_bounded: A named nonzero defect is bounded, with threshold significance left open.
values.adaptive: Agreement is maintained or approached through ongoing adjustment rather than one fixed copy map.

fidelity.blocked: Exactness at one granularity does not imply exactness of the full package or lineage.

reversibility.question: Does the protocol expose an inverse at the declared granularity?

values.reversible: A declared inverse route recovers the named object exactly within its admissible domain.
values.approximately_reversible: A reverse route recovers the named object only up to a declared residual/equivalence.
values.irreversible: No admissible inverse is stipulated for the named object.

reversibility.blocked: Protocol reversibility does not entail token identity or zero route holonomy for unmeasured structures.

route_multiplicity.question: How many admissible routes connect the declared operational endpoints?

values.unique_route: Only one route is admitted at the scenario's declared resolution.
values.multiple_equivalent_routes: Several routes are stipulated to agree under a named endpoint comparison, with stronger equivalence left open.
values.holonomy_bearing_routes: Closed or alternative routes can restore selected endpoint observables while changing another declared structure.

route_multiplicity.blocked: One successful route does not establish route independence; endpoint agreement does not erase route history.

granularity.question: At what level is the scenario's stipulated fidelity/comparison made?

values.predictive_state: Future-sufficient classes, transition structure, or continuation-relevant state.
values.package_state: A multi-clause package record or maintained package-level structure.
values.event_package: Globally packaged event/role/time/identity structure rather than pairwise local records.
values.certificate_only: Only a declared certificate, report, or externally decoded signature is matched.

granularity.blocked: Agreement at a coarser granularity cannot be promoted to a finer one without a theorem.

discriminators.name: predictive_fiber_continuity
discriminators.label: Continuity of predictive fibers
discriminators.question: Does the candidate relate source and target future-sufficient classes, rather than only current/public states?

discriminators.name: admissible_continuation_structure
discriminators.label: Preservation of admissible continuation structure

discriminators.name: temporal_overlap_and_causal_coupling
discriminators.label: Temporal overlap and causal coupling
discriminators.question: Which causal/process dependence and clock relation connects source, bridge stages, and target?

discriminators.name: recombination_content
discriminators.label: Survival of recombination content

discriminators.name: ledger_and_viability_continuity

discriminators.name: lineage_cardinality_and_uniqueness
discriminators.label: Uniqueness or branching of continuation
discriminators.question: Does the criterion return zero, one, many, or fused successors, and what breaks symmetry or yields underdetermination?

scenarios.title: Gradual component-by-component replacement
scenarios.canonical_prompt: Gradual neuron-by-neuron or component-by-component replacement.
scenarios.purpose: Isolate staged responsibility transfer, overlap, order effects, and the difference between local replacement success and a globally maintained package.
facts: Source-side components are retired in a declared sequence while target-side components assume corresponding operational roles.
At least one interval contains contributions from both separately typed supports.
Each local replacement is stipulated to meet a declared local interface test; full-package preservation is not stipulated.
The source contribution decreases over stages, and a final source-withdrawal intervention is available.
scenarios.episode_graph: E_S^0 -> E_mix^1 -> ... -> E_mix^n -> E_T^n
scenarios.branch_graph: operational 1->1 with mixed-support intermediate episodes
scenarios.clock_relation: shared route order; local clocks need not be identical
scenarios.causal_structure: continuous coupled process with moving support responsibility
scenarios.fidelity_scope: local role/interface tests plus an adaptive package-level trajectory; hidden/predictive equivalence remains open
scenarios.autonomy_intervention: remove every remaining source-side contribution and transfer controller after the final scheduled stage
scenarios.instrument_constraints: local tests may be public or privileged; global hidden/predictive state need not be observable
variants: brief versus long overlap per component
exact local tests versus residual-bounded local tests
stress_questions: Do all admissible replacement orders yield equivalent target package data?
Can every local handoff pass while no global package exists at an intermediate stage?
Which source-specific history is carried by mixed-support episodes rather than reconstructed at the end?
Does final source withdrawal expose protocol dependence that was hidden during overlap?
blocked_inferences: Graduality is not continuity by definition.
Overlap is not token identity.
Local test success is not global package preservation.
A smooth public trajectory is not predictive-fiber continuity.

scenarios.title: Instantaneous destructive scan and reconstruction
scenarios.canonical_prompt: Instantaneous destructive scan and reconstruction.
scenarios.purpose: Separate exact record reconstruction from causal overlap, source persistence, and any assumed lineage effect of destruction.
facts: A source record is acquired at one declared resolution and the source package/support is made unavailable before target activation.
A disjoint target is constructed from the retained record in one unresolved translation stage.
The target is stipulated exact at the declared microstate record, but continuation laws and full-package gates are candidate questions.
No source-target operating overlap is stipulated.
scenarios.episode_graph: E_S --scan/erase--> R --reconstruct--> E_T
scenarios.branch_graph: operational 1->record->1
scenarios.clock_relation: source endpoint precedes target start; no shared now required
scenarios.causal_structure: record-mediated source-to-target dependence without live overlap
scenarios.fidelity_scope: exact retained scan record only; no automatic predictive, package, or lineage exactness
scenarios.autonomy_intervention: remove the scan record, reconstruction machinery, and source-side resources after activation
scenarios.instrument_constraints: complete scan-record access is stipulated; hidden dynamics not encoded in the record remain open
variants: record includes transition law versus state only
source erased during versus immediately after scan
stress_questions: Does exact microstate reconstruction induce a well-defined history/continuation bridge?
Which conclusion changes solely because the source is erased before activation?
Can a candidate distinguish reconstruction from continuation without smuggling token identity into the record?
What target-native maintenance remains after reconstruction equipment is removed?
blocked_inferences: Source destruction is not proof of target lineage.
Microstate equality under a record map is not cross-typed token equality.
A record is not a dormant subject by definition.
No overlap is not discontinuity under every criterion.

scenarios.title: Nondestructive exact copy while source continues
scenarios.canonical_prompt: Nondestructive exact copy while the source continues.
scenarios.purpose: Expose the difference between exact structural duplication, source persistence, branch cardinality, and unique-continuation claims.
facts: One disjoint target is activated while the source remains active.
Source and target are stipulated exact at the declared package-state comparison at the split instant.
After activation, source and target receive independently selectable continuations.
The copying bridge can be removed without changing the fact that both live episodes exist; post-removal maintenance remains to be tested.
scenarios.branch_graph: one pre-copy episode to two simultaneously live episodes
scenarios.clock_relation: split event plus independent post-split local times
scenarios.causal_structure: common causal ancestry followed by independent dynamics
scenarios.fidelity_scope: exact package-state relation at split; future equivalence after divergent inputs is not stipulated
scenarios.autonomy_intervention: remove copy machinery and any shared synchronization channel while keeping ordinary environments
scenarios.instrument_constraints: exact package access at split is stipulated; future hidden state may diverge under different continuations
variants: copy bridge removed immediately versus later
stress_questions: Can a criterion select one unique successor without an asymmetric fact?
Does source persistence alter lineage or only reveal branching that was already implicit?
Are both post-split episodes successors, or is lineage undefined/underdetermined?
What structures remain exact after independently controlled futures?
blocked_inferences: Exact duplication is not unique continuation.
A duplicate is not nonreal by definition.
Source persistence is not proof that only the source continues.
Common ancestry is not token identity.

scenarios.title: Copy first, source deletion later
scenarios.canonical_prompt: Copy first, source deletion later.
scenarios.purpose: Test whether lineage classifications illegitimately change retroactively when a source is deleted after a period of coactivation.
facts: A target is created while the source continues, and both operate for a declared overlap interval.
The target is exact at the declared package-state comparison at activation.
The source is erased only after source and target have accumulated distinguishable post-copy histories.
The target remains available for a withdrawal/autonomy test after deletion.
scenarios.branch_graph: one-to-many split followed by removal of the source-side branch
scenarios.clock_relation: shared split marker; independent histories before deletion
scenarios.causal_structure: copy ancestry, independent coactivity, then exogenous source removal
scenarios.fidelity_scope: exact at copy instant only; histories differ before source deletion
scenarios.autonomy_intervention: source deletion is one intervention; separately remove any remaining copy/synchronization apparatus
scenarios.instrument_constraints: both branch histories are available in the thought experiment
variants: deletion chosen by source versus external operator
source branch damaged versus clean at deletion
stress_questions: Can deletion at time t change the lineage relation assigned at the earlier split?
Does the target acquire uniqueness only because a competing branch is removed?
Which branch-specific histories matter after deletion?
Is source deletion part of handoff, autonomy testing, lineage evidence, or all three separately?
blocked_inferences: Later deletion does not retroactively erase a prior branch.
Being the sole survivor is not unique lineage by definition.
Source erasure is not an ontological transfer event.
Target availability is not target autonomy.

scenarios.title: Two simultaneous exact targets
scenarios.canonical_prompt: Two simultaneous exact targets.
scenarios.purpose: Create a maximally symmetric duplication case that tests unique-lineage rules and hidden tie-breakers.
facts: Two disjoint target carriers are activated simultaneously from the same source-side record/process.
The two targets are stipulated isomorphic and exact at the declared package-state comparison at activation.
No target-distinguishing causal, temporal, spatial-priority, naming, or quality fact is admitted at the split.
The source is erased before joint activation to prevent source persistence from being the sole asymmetry.
scenarios.episode_graph: E_S -> erase; R -> {E_T1, E_T2} (symmetric)
scenarios.branch_graph: one source record to two symmetry-related targets
scenarios.clock_relation: joint activation under a symmetry-preserving clock relation
scenarios.causal_structure: equal common ancestry with no admitted asymmetry between target legs
scenarios.fidelity_scope: exact package-state match on both legs at activation
scenarios.autonomy_intervention: remove common reconstruction/synchronization support from both targets symmetrically
scenarios.instrument_constraints: complete declared structural access; target labels are treated as gauge-like names for symmetry testing
variants: a tiny asymmetry is introduced only after activation
stress_questions: What non-arbitrary fact could select exactly one target?
Does the candidate return two successors, no unique successor, or token-level underdetermination?
Would relabeling T1 and T2 change the verdict?
Can later divergence or failure determine an earlier lineage fact without retroactivity?
blocked_inferences: Numerical multiplicity is not nonrealization.
Symmetry cannot be broken by names alone.
Source deletion does not select one target.
Exact package equivalence does not resolve token identity.

scenarios.title: Target activation after a temporal gap
scenarios.canonical_prompt: Target activation after a temporal gap.
scenarios.purpose: Separate a dormant record/restart protocol from uninterrupted activity and force explicit temporal-lineage semantics.
facts: The source is paused or made unavailable after producing a retained checkpoint record.
A nonzero interval contains no stipulated active full package on source or target.
A disjoint target is later activated exactly from the checkpoint at the declared predictive-state granularity.
The record persists through the gap; whether anything else persists is not stipulated.
scenarios.episode_graph: E_S -> checkpoint R -> [gap: no active package stipulated] -> E_T
scenarios.branch_graph: one active episode, one inert record interval, one target episode
scenarios.clock_relation: partial order with a gap; no canonical phase alignment unless supplied
scenarios.causal_structure: record-mediated dependence across an inactive interval
scenarios.fidelity_scope: exact predictive checkpoint as defined by the scenario; temporal closure and full package are open
scenarios.autonomy_intervention: remove checkpoint store and restart controller after target activation
scenarios.instrument_constraints: checkpoint contents are available; no observation during the inactive gap can certify an active package
variants: source can versus cannot be resumed
checkpoint stores state only versus transition/ledger history
stress_questions: What object, if any, carries lineage through an interval with no active package?
Is the checkpoint a bridge record, a package component, or only a reconstruction resource?
Does gap duration matter if the structural record is unchanged?
Can temporal closure be re-established without being preserved continuously?
blocked_inferences: A stored record is not an active package by definition.
Temporal gap is not extinction under every lineage criterion.
Exact restart is not uninterrupted causal activity.
Dormancy and reconstruction require separate classification.

scenarios.title: Long-lived source-target overlap
scenarios.canonical_prompt: Transfer through a long-lived source-target overlap.
scenarios.purpose: Test process-level handoff, moving responsibility, source-target coupling, and whether overlap hides dependence rather than establishing autonomy.
facts: Separately typed source and target supports operate jointly for a long interval.
Package functions are reassigned gradually, but both sides remain causally coupled through most of the route.
A target-dominant episode is reached before source-side support is finally removed.
The protocol adaptively corrects discrepancies during overlap.
scenarios.episode_graph: E_S -> E_joint^1 -> ... -> E_joint^m(target-dominant) -> E_T?
scenarios.branch_graph: one coupled operational trajectory with changing contribution weights
scenarios.clock_relation: coupled clocks during overlap; independent target clock after withdrawal
scenarios.causal_structure: continuous bidirectional or feedback coupling during overlap
scenarios.fidelity_scope: adaptive package-level agreement under coupled operation
scenarios.autonomy_intervention: remove all source-target coupling channels and source-side repair/control after target-dominant operation stabilizes
scenarios.instrument_constraints: joint operation can mask which side generates the observed package behavior
variants: withdrawal before versus after target repair internalization
stress_questions: Which package predicates are genuinely target-native before withdrawal?
Can contribution weights define handoff without defining identity?
Does long overlap provide evidence unavailable in an abrupt protocol, or merely more opportunity for external correction?
What fails first when coupling is removed?
blocked_inferences: Long overlap is not autonomy.
Continuous coupling is not one carrier unless explicitly retyped.
Target dominance is not exclusive realization.
Adaptive correction can be externally supplied.

scenarios.title: Distributed extension with no sharp handoff
scenarios.canonical_prompt: Distributed extension in which no sharp handoff exists.
scenarios.purpose: Challenge source-target narratives that require an exclusive transfer instant when a package remains jointly distributed.
facts: A source package is extended onto additional target-side support while source-side support remains a permanent active component.
No stage is designated as the unique handoff or as a target-only episode.
The declared package is jointly organized across supports and may fail if either side is removed.
Operational responsibility changes, but the joint boundary remains the candidate package boundary.
scenarios.episode_graph: E_S -> E_joint -> E_joint' -> ... (no target-only node stipulated)
scenarios.branch_graph: one joint distributed package assembled from multiple support episodes
scenarios.clock_relation: partially synchronized distributed clocks
scenarios.causal_structure: permanent joint causal organization
scenarios.fidelity_scope: joint package behavior; no target-only package is stipulated
scenarios.autonomy_intervention: remove one support partition at a time and test whether the remaining assembly still satisfies the declared package
scenarios.instrument_constraints: observations of the joint assembly may not localize package predicates to either support
variants: source contribution tends to zero without reaching zero
joint package with modular versus inseparable clauses
stress_questions: Must a candidate force this case into source and target tokens, or may the joint package be the only valid object?
Is lineage applicable when no target-only episode exists?
Does permanent bridge dependence indicate failure, or simply define the distributed package boundary?
How are C-clause carriers typed when different clauses live on different supports?
blocked_inferences: No sharp handoff does not imply no structural change.
Permanent coupling is not automatically counterfeit.
Distributed realization does not specify one or many subjects.
A joint carrier cannot be assumed without declaring its support and interfaces.

scenarios.title: Fission followed by independent divergence
scenarios.canonical_prompt: Fission followed by independent divergence.
scenarios.purpose: Force relation-valued or branch-sensitive lineage semantics and expose the loss of a single future after a common split.
facts: One source episode produces two target episodes exact at the declared package state at the split.
The source-side episode is then removed, and the two targets receive different admissible continuations.
Branch histories diverge in predictive state, action-credit ledger, and possibly viability outcomes.
No later fusion is stipulated.
scenarios.branch_graph: 1->2 with independent post-split histories
scenarios.clock_relation: common split coordinate followed by independent clocks
scenarios.causal_structure: shared prehistory, equal split ancestry, then causally separate branches
scenarios.fidelity_scope: exact at branch point; divergence is stipulated afterward
scenarios.autonomy_intervention: remove common bridge and source resources, then test branches independently
scenarios.instrument_constraints: both branch histories and target package records are available
variants: branches retain versus erase common-prehistory markers
stress_questions: Can one source have two legitimate successors without violating the candidate's ontology-free structural rules?
Which common-prehistory facts remain well-defined after divergent futures?
Does branch failure affect the status of the other branch?
Can action-credit be duplicated, divided, or only related by ancestry?
blocked_inferences: Fission does not force a function-valued lineage.
Divergence does not retroactively remove common ancestry.
One branch's failure does not select the other as uniquely original.
Shared prehistory is not shared token identity.

scenarios.title: Fission followed by later fusion
scenarios.canonical_prompt: Fission followed by later fusion.
scenarios.purpose: Probe whether branch histories and recombination content can be coherently merged, lost, or retained in a many-to-one target.
facts: One source fissions into two exact-at-split branches that later acquire nonidentical histories.
A fusion bridge combines both branch records/processes into one target episode.
The target may match selected branchwise summaries while joint/recombination facts remain a separate question.
The two branch episodes are retired after fusion.
scenarios.branch_graph: 1->2->1 with route-sensitive branch histories
scenarios.clock_relation: branch-local clocks require a fusion synchronization/ordering rule
scenarios.causal_structure: two causally independent branch histories jointly feed one fusion process
scenarios.fidelity_scope: adaptive event/package synthesis from two nonidentical branch histories
scenarios.autonomy_intervention: retire both branch sources and fusion controller, then test the fused target
scenarios.instrument_constraints: branchwise summaries may be observable while cross-branch recombination content may require privileged audit
stress_questions: What source-specific facts can the fused target inherit when branch histories conflict?
Does fusion order create holonomy or different target package states?
Can pairwise branch-to-target matches exist without one globally coherent fusion package?
Does the lineage relation allow multiple predecessors without asserting token identity with all of them?
blocked_inferences: Fusion is not identity with every source branch.
Matching branchwise summaries is not preservation of recombination content.
A single final target does not make the route one-to-one.
Conflict resolution is a substantive rule, not a bookkeeping detail.

scenarios.title: Public-perfect copy with predictive mismatch
scenarios.canonical_prompt: Public/report-perfect copy with predictive mismatch.
scenarios.purpose: Serve as a counterfeit control demonstrating that current/report equivalence can leave future-sufficient structure different.
facts: A disjoint target matches every declared current public/report observable of the source over the stipulated test set.
A privileged continuation test reveals different predictive classes or transition responses.
The source remains active so both systems can be probed under matched and divergent continuations.
The mismatch is a scenario input fact, not an outcome label or ontological judgment.

Counterfeit is a named structural control, not a claim of phenomenal absence.
Behavioral indistinguishability under one test set is not global identity.

scenarios.title: Predictive match with different binding or action-credit structure
scenarios.canonical_prompt: Predictive match with different binding or action-credit structure.
scenarios.purpose: Prevent predictive equivalence from being silently upgraded to full package equivalence or preserved mineness/provenance.
facts: A disjoint target matches the source's declared predictive quotient and transition responses.
Privileged audit shows a different binding relation, action-credit ledger, or source-provenance structure.
The source remains active during comparison.
The mismatch concerns a named package clause or cross-clause relation, not an untyped essence.

scenarios.branch_graph: source plus one predictive-matching target

scenarios.instrument_constraints: predictive interface alone cannot detect the stipulated binding/credit mismatch

scenarios.title: Target maintained only by an external decoder or source process
scenarios.canonical_prompt: Target maintained only by an external decoder or source process.
scenarios.purpose: Distinguish target-native realization and autonomy from an externally generated readout or continuously reconstructed shadow.

blocked_inferences: One-cycle closeness is not stable approximation.
Approximate inverse is not flat transport.
Public tolerance does not bound hidden drift.

scenarios.title: Dormant backup activated after source erasure
scenarios.canonical_prompt: A target backup is created while the source lives, remains inert for a long interval, and activates only after source erasure.
scenarios.purpose: Distinguish creation time, activation time, causal provenance, temporal gap, and the possibility of a dormant but nonoperating target structure.
facts: A disjoint target backup is written from the source and then kept dynamically inert.
The source continues and acquires new history not included in the backup.
The source is later erased; after another interval the old backup is activated.
The activated target exactly matches the source only at backup time and is otherwise historically stale.
scenarios.episode_graph: E_S(t0) -> dormant B_T; E_S(t1) erased; gap; B_T activates as E_T
scenarios.branch_graph: source continues beyond backup fork; dormant target later activates
scenarios.clock_relation: backup snapshot time, source terminal time, and target activation time are distinct
scenarios.causal_structure: source-derived dormant record with missing post-backup causal history
scenarios.fidelity_scope: exact at snapshot predictive state but lossy relative to the source terminal episode
scenarios.autonomy_intervention: remove restoration service and all source archives after activation
scenarios.instrument_constraints: target may report snapshot-consistent history while lacking later source events
stress_questions: Which source time is the candidate's lineage endpoint?
Does a dormant record participate in lineage before activation?
How is missing post-backup action-credit history represented?
Does later source erasure alter the backup's earlier status?
blocked_inferences: A backup is not an active target episode by definition.
Later activation does not retroactively include missing history.
Source erasure does not update a stale record.
Snapshot fidelity is time-indexed.

scenarios.title: Overlap transfer that degrades the source
scenarios.canonical_prompt: Source-target coupling improves target fidelity while progressively damaging the source package.
scenarios.purpose: Test whether a candidate tracks asymmetric costs, source-side viability, and whether target success can coexist with source failure during overlap.
facts: A temporary bridge couples source and target during transfer.
Each transfer stage improves a declared target fidelity measure but consumes or perturbs source resources.
The source crosses a viability/package boundary before final target handoff.
The target may or may not be autonomous after bridge withdrawal; that remains a separate test.
scenarios.episode_graph: E_S viable + E_T immature -> coupled transfer -> E_S fails; E_T candidate
scenarios.branch_graph: one source-target coupled trajectory with source-side terminal failure
scenarios.clock_relation: shared transfer stages plus separate source/target viability times
scenarios.causal_structure: directed resource/information extraction with asymmetric disturbance
scenarios.fidelity_scope: target fidelity rises under a source-cost ledger; no conservation or identity interpretation is built in
scenarios.autonomy_intervention: withdraw bridge immediately after source failure and audit target maintenance
scenarios.instrument_constraints: target-facing success metrics can hide source-side degradation unless both ledgers are observed
variants: target fidelity saturates before source failure
stress_questions: Does source failure have any formal effect on target lineage, or only on protocol ethics/cost?
Can target fidelity be purchased by erasing source predictive information?
Which ledger records the transfer's asymmetric resource use?
Does target maintenance continue without the damaged source?
blocked_inferences: Source damage is not evidence of target continuation.
A costly process is not necessarily more identity-preserving.
Target success does not imply source preservation.
Source terminal failure does not establish target autonomy.

scenarios.title: Replacement-order critical pair
scenarios.canonical_prompt: Two locally admissible replacement orders reach publicly identical endpoints but differ in hidden/package residue.
scenarios.purpose: Provide a minimal confluence and path-independence test for gradual transfer protocols.
facts: Two source components A and B can each be replaced by target components A' and B' using locally admissible steps.
Route r1 replaces A then B; route r2 replaces B then A.
Both routes yield the same declared public endpoint and carrier inventory.
A predictive, memory, action-credit, or binding residue differs unless an additional commutation/confluence condition holds.
scenarios.episode_graph: S --replace A--> X --replace B--> T; S --replace B--> Y --replace A--> T'
scenarios.branch_graph: one source with two protocol routes to endpoint-equivalent targets
scenarios.clock_relation: two stage orders with comparable endpoints but different intermediate histories
scenarios.causal_structure: noncommuting local updates under a shared public endpoint comparison
scenarios.fidelity_scope: exact public endpoint and local step tests; global predictive/package equality is not stipulated
scenarios.autonomy_intervention: remove all source/bridge components after each route and compare target-native maintenance
scenarios.instrument_constraints: endpoint-only audits miss route residue; intermediate and recombination probes are required
stress_questions: What condition makes the replacement system confluent on the transported object?
Can route-dependent endpoints receive different lineage verdicts despite public equality?
Which hidden residue is operationally detectable by recombination or future continuation?
Does autonomy differ across the two routes?
blocked_inferences: Same endpoint inventory is not same transported object.
Local admissibility is not confluence.
Gradual replacement order is not automatically irrelevant.
A path-independent public shadow can conceal holonomy.
